skill.name: writing-video-prompts
skill.description: Writes the motion prompt for a video clip — what moves, how the camera behaves, the physics and the audio, in the shape the chosen model wants. Works from a brief alone, from a start frame, from a source video, or from a storyboard sheet where each panel becomes a cut. Handles one clip or a whole set, returning one prompt per clip. Nothing is generated here. Use when a clip's model, duration and content are settled and it needs the prompt written.
skill.summary: Writes model-specific motion, camera, timing, and audio prompts for individual video clips.
skill.author: supercmohq

content.user_title: Write Precise Video Prompts for Every Clip
content.value_statement: Generic prompts often produce weak motion, inconsistent framing, and poorly synchronized audio. This skill writes structured clip prompts for specific video models and supplied media.
actual_capabilities: Writes one motion prompt for each clip in a video brief.
Adapts prompt structure for Seedance, Veo, Gemini Omni, Kling, Grok, and Wan model families.
Converts storyboard panels into timed cuts while preserving visible composition and object positions.
Directs camera movement, physical action, performance, dialogue, ambience, and sound effects.
Labels start frames, end frames, source videos, people, products, and reference media according to each model guide.
Checks beat duration, hand usage, continuity, and physical action before returning prompts.
limitations: The skill writes prompt text but does not generate or render video.
Reliable storyboard interpretation requires access to image analysis.
Models outside the included families require separate model capability information.
Generated video quality still depends on the selected model, source media, duration, and content restrictions.

use_cases.title: Direct Product Clips
use_cases.description: Turn product actions, references, and dialogue into precise prompts that protect labels, object state, and hand continuity.

use_cases.title: Convert Storyboards
use_cases.description: Translate each storyboard panel into a timed cut with matching framing, motion, performance, and audio direction.

use_cases.title: Adapt Prompts Across Models
use_cases.description: Rewrite a settled clip brief using the structure, labels, timing, and audio syntax expected by a chosen model.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Single Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a video prompt for a [duration] clip using [model]. The subject is [subject], and the main action is [action]. Use [camera move] with [audio requirements].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple brief that has one subject and one continuous action.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Start Frame
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a [model] prompt that begins from my supplied frame. Preserve [fixed details]. Animate [motion] over [duration] with [camera behavior] and [sound].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a fixed opening composition while directing only the motion and changes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this storyboard and write one [model] prompt for a [duration] clip. Make each panel a cut. Match visible framing, hands, products, expressions, dialogue, and audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate several panels into a timed sequence with hard cuts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Clip Prompt Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Write prompts for all clips in this video plan using [model]. Keep [shared look] and [aspect ratio] consistent. Validate timing, continuity, media labels, dialogue segmentation, and model-specific syntax.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an advanced prompt package for several independent clips in one production.

output_examples.input: Create a six-second Veo clip of a ceramic cup filling with coffee during a slow push-in.
output_examples.output: Close-up, slow push-in. A white ceramic cup rests beneath the brewer as a steady coffee stream fills it. Warm morning light crosses the counter. SFX: coffee pours into ceramic. Ambient noise: quiet kitchen room tone.

output_examples.input: Animate a start frame of a runner at sunrise for Wan 2.7, with footsteps and no cut.
output_examples.output: The runner is already moving along the empty track at sunrise. Their stride remains steady as the camera tracks beside them in one continuous medium shot. Each footfall lands firmly on the rubber surface. Crisp footsteps and light morning wind follow the motion.

best_practices: Provide the target model, clip duration, main action, media roles, and exact dialogue before requesting the prompt.
Keep each beat focused on one continuous action and one clear camera movement.
Review timing, physical continuity, reference labels, and audio markers before rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated actions or several camera moves inside one short beat.
Do not restate every visible detail from a supplied frame or storyboard.
Do not ask this skill to generate the finished video or guarantee model output quality.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos?
faq.answer: No. It returns written prompts for video-generation models.

faq.question: Which video models have dedicated guidance?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Seedance 2.0, Veo 3.1, Gemini Omni, Kling 3.0, Grok Imagine Video, and Wan 2.7 families.

faq.question: Can it work from a storyboard?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map each panel to a cut after the storyboard image is analyzed.

faq.question: Can it use start frames and reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. It labels supported media and writes motion that respects the fixed visual information.

faq.question: How does it handle dialogue and sound?
faq.answer: It preserves exact dialogue, divides speech across beats, and uses each model's required audio notation.

faq.question: What happens when the brief has too many beats?
faq.answer: It reports the timing conflict and returns only the beats that can fit without harmful compression.
